EXTRACT FROM DAILY INTELLIGENCE REPORT DATED 29/3/32

Unemployed workers of Japanese mills - meetings in the
Western District.

It is reported that 20 unemployed workers of Japanese
cotton mills held a meeting on a piece of vacant ground to
the east of North Ying Hwa Li, off Robison Road, between
12 noon and 2 p.m. March 28, when Li San ( 李山 ), an
ex-worker of the N.W.K. No.8 Mill, presided. The following
resolutions were discussed and passed :-

1. That Pao Wen Tseng ( 包文增 ), alias Pao Lao-sz ( 包老四 ),
native of Kiangsu and owner of Pao Yung Shing ( 包永兴 )
Coffin Shop, Ferry Road, be severely dealt with for being
a running dog of the Japanese and a traitor to the Chinese.

2. That all ex-workers be notified to secure batons and
sticks for the purpose of assaulting at the entrance of
various Japanese mills, traitorous strike-breakers.

At the conclusion of the meeting, copies of a
mosquito paper entitled "Sing Pao" ( 新报 ) (Vide I.R.26/3/32)
Issue No.3, were distributed among the attendance. In
addition to the usual seditious propaganda matter, it
contains an article alleging that the lower rank officers and
soldiers of the Kuomintang Army being enraged at the non-
resistance policy have declared their intention to join
the Communist Party. This expression, it continues, shows
that the soldiers have realized that only the Communist Party
is opposing Imperialism.

J.B.S 2/4

J.I. Kuh.
Report early please.
J.B.S 2/4

日本纱厂失业工人——西区集会。

据报，3月28日中午12时至下午2时之间，约20名日本棉纺厂失业工人在罗宾森路（Robison Road）北英华里以东的一块空地上举行会议，前西北织造厂第八厂工人李山（Li San）担任主席。讨论并通过了以下决议：-

1. 江苏籍人士、渡船路包永兴棺材店店主包文增（Pao Wen Tseng），别名包老四（Pao Lao-sz），因充当日本人的走狗及汉奸，应予以严厉惩处。

2. 通知所有前工人准备棍棒和木条，以便在各日本工厂入口处袭击背叛罢工的工贼。

会议结束时，向与会者分发了一份名为《新报》（Sing Pao）的小报第3期（参见1932年3月26日情报报告）。除了通常的煽动性宣传内容外，该报还刊登了一篇文章，声称国民党军队的下级军官和士兵因不满不抵抗政策而愤怒，已宣布打算加入共产党。文章接着称，这一表态表明士兵们已经认识到只有共产党在反对帝国主义。

J.B.S 4月2日

侦探员 顾（Kuh）。
请尽早提交报告。
J.B.S 4月2日

EXTRACT FROM DAILY INTELLIGENCE REPORT DATED 26/3/32

Pro-communistic propaganda sold in the Eastern District
Copies of pro-communistic newspaper entitled "Sing
Pao" (新報), Issue No.2, dated March 25, bearing an
address "5249 Avenue Haig" were surreptitiously sold
by hawkers on Rangoon Road on March 25. Apart from
the usual reactionary articles, the paper contains a song
praising the brave peasants and an item urging the people
to overthrow the Kuomintang control.

JBB 2/4

3月25日，小贩在兰贡路（Rangoon Road）秘密出售题为《新报》（Sing Pao）的亲共报纸第2期，日期为3月25日，地址标注为“海格路5249号”。除了通常的反动文章外，该报还包含一首赞美勇敢农民的歌曲，以及一项呼吁民众推翻国民党统治的内容。

Special Branch S.1. Station,
REPORT
Date March 23, 19 32.

Subject (in full) Secret Subversive base

Made by D.I. Sih Tsz-liang Forwarded by Jhn Robertson, Supt

I beg to report that Agent Chang Ching-foh
(張金福) of S. 1 has received from an informer information
of a secret address, where subversive activities are planned,
in a Chinese old style unnumbered house at the corner of
Ferry and Macao Roads, (sketch showing the location attached).
According to the Agent this is the place where the so-called
pickets of the Japanese Cotton Mills receive every day their
maintenance fee. The time when these pickets go there is
from 8-9 a.m. every day. Copies of a mosquito newspaper
entitled "Sin Pao" a copy of which is attached, containing
articles such as "The American Imperialists are assisting
Chiang Kai-shek to attack the Red Army" etc., are at present
believed to be stored there.

Sih Tse Liang
D. I.

Officer i/c Special Branch.

SECRET - NOT FOR PRESS PUBLICATION
MUNICIPAL POLICE (SPECIAL BRANCH) - INTELLIGENCE SUMMARY 30/3/32.
（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE C. & S. B. REGISTRY No. D 32554 Date 1/4/32.）

1. Citizens' Federation - 20th Branch Association - Meeting
Some 60 members of the abovementioned Association with an office at 506 Kwangsi Road at a meeting held in the Mei Yuan Restaurant, 369 Foochow Road, between 3.30 and 4.30 p.m. March 29, decided to submit the following two suggestions to the Citizens' Federation :-
1. That rentals be reduced by 50%.
2. That the Municipality of Greater Shanghai be requested to instruct all banks to make loans to the people in order to relieve the presnt the prsent local economic stringency.

2. Chamber of Commerce issues poster calling for resumption of business
Copies of a poster, a translation of which is as follows, were found exhibited on various principal thoroughfares in the Settlement, the French Concession and Nantao on the morning of March 30 :-
"Notification of the Shanghai Municipality Chamber of Commerce"
"With a view to diminishing the unemployment terror, stabilizing the financial situation of the locality and restoring the income of the Government treasury, thus increasing the strength of the lengthy resistance against disgrace, all shops and factories in the safe districts which have not resumed operation, should recommence business forthwith in accordance with the notice of this Chamber on March 1".

3. Japanese Schools to re-open
The School Committee of the Shanghai Japanese Residents' Corporation has tentatively decided to re-open all schools under its control on Monday, April 11.

1. 市民联合会 - 第20支部协会 - 会议
上述协会约有60名成员，其办公室位于广西路506号，于3月29日下午3时30分至4时30分在福州路369号梅园酒家举行会议，决定向市民联合会提交以下两项建议：-
1. 租金减少50%。
2. 请求大上海市政府指令所有银行向民众发放贷款，以缓解当前当地的经济紧缩状况。

2. 商会发布海报呼吁复工

4. Western District Unemployed workers - Meeting
It is reported that some 40 unemployed workers of the Western
District at a meeting held in No.5 House, Lanc No.7 of the Doong
Shing Mill Labour Quarters, Macao Road, between 6 and 7 p.m.
March 29 when Wong Ts Hung (王志红), an ex-worker of the afore
mentioned mill presided. A general discussion took place and
the following decisions were reached:-
1. That a general meeting of unemployed workers be convened at 10
a.m. March 30 on a vacant piece of ground to the east of Ferry
Road and south of Macao Road (the place is known as Tso Ah Fang)
(草鞋浜) with a view to welcoming a labour representative from
Kiangsi.
All 2. That the whole body of unemployed workers be instructed to pro-
ceed at 9 a.m. April 2 to the Shanghai Special District Court
with a view to demanding the release of all arrested unemployed
workers.
3. That pickets be sent on the evening of March 30 to the vicinity
of Pao Yung Shing (包永兴) Coffin Shop, Ferry Rd., with a view
to assaulting its proprietor Pao Lau-s (包老四), and his Kiangsu
followers who are "running dogs" of the Japanese and were
responsible for an assault upon workers' pickets at 6 p.m. Mar.25.

5.Rice Hong owners - Meeting
Twenty-three owners of Chapei Rice hongs held a meeting in the
temporary office of their association, 1153 Peking Road, between
2.30 and 4 p.m. Mar. 29 and passed the following resolutions:-
1. That arrangement be made to rent a place in the vicinity of
the corner of Chekiang and Soochow Roads for the purpose
of organizing a rice bazaar for the Chapei rice hong owners
to resume business on April 1.
2. That representatives be sent to the S.M.C. to arrange for
the landing of rice at jetties on the Soochow Creek.

THE CHINA PRESS, THURSDAY, MARCH 31, 1932
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
& S. B. REGISTRY.
D 9255 A
1. 4. 32.

Jobless Plan
Mass Meeting
Here Saturday
Chinese Merchants Seek
Exemption From Police
Tax In Hongkew

Unemployed workers at the Western district of Shanghai yesterday were completing arrangements for the holding of a monster mass meeting of unemployed persons, one object being to march in a body to Shanghai Special District Court on Saturday for the purpose of demanding that all unemployed persons under detention be released at once.

The initial meeting of persons arranging for the mass meeting was held in House No. 8, Lane No. 7 of the Dong Sheng Mill labor quarters, off Maopo Road, on Tuesday.

Wong Ta-tsang, a former employee at the mill, presided. Following general discussions arrangements were completed for the holding of another meeting at which plans are to be completed.

Police Will Halt Parade

It is expected that International Settlement police will interfere in the event the unemployed persons attempt to march through the Settlement without the necessary permit, or if they attempt to hold a demonstration.

Yesterday a large number of unemployed persons held a mass meeting in a vacant piece of ground east of Ferry and south of Macao Roads, at which time they extended a welcome to a labor delegate from Nanking.

Tax Exemption Sought

Chinese business men here are seeking for the exemption of paying the police tax in the Hongkew District before opening their shops tomorrow and in the second meeting of the Business Resumption Committee yesterday afternoon decided to petition the Shanghai Municipal Council for exemption.

As to the protection of Chinese shops in that district the committee also obtained orally with a guarantee from Mr. Stirling Fessenden, secretary general of the Council, whom they visited.

Both the Chinese Ratepayers Association and Real Estate Owners Association were entrusted with the mission of drafting a plan whereby merchants in Hongkew can best be relieved of financial difficulties and while shopkeepers in other parts of the city may be required to pay rentals the Hongkew men may enjoy entire exemption, it was said.

In all Chinese vernacular papers today there will appear a long declaration by Chinese merchant bodies mentioning all events leading up to the resumption of business besides a brief notice stating that all shops will be opened tomorrow. In the declaration both Nanking and the Shanghai Municipal Council are criticized for inadequate protection for Chinese merchants during the recent Sino-Japanese conflict here.

Factories Reopen

With the reopening of 20 mills and factories closed since the opening guns of the Sino-Japanese conflict here, a total of 112 manufacturing concerns have now opened their doors since the outbreak of hostilities.

Additional reopenings are expected April 1, the date set by the Chinese Chamber of Commerce for the resumption of business by Chinese concerns in the safer districts of Shanghai.

Pensions Ask Resumption

Former employees from the Chinese chamber in connection with the resumption of business on April 1 appeared in the Settlement and Concession yesterday. They read: with a view to diminishing unemployment, stabilizing finances in this locality and restoring the income of the national government treasury, thus increasing the strength of the resistance against disgrace, all shops and factories in safe districts which have not resumed business should do so April 1.

Former employees of Japanese mills, in anticipation of their re-opening, have drawn up the following list of demands and conditions which they will consider returning to the employ of Japanese mill owners:

1. The issue of a monthly bonus equivalent to four days' wages. This to be paid before resumption of work.
2. Full wage issue for the period of the closing.
3. Full pay for Sunday holiday and double pay for other holidays when the mills resume open.
4. An increase of $5 for all earning less than $30 per month, and an increase of $3 for all earning more than $30 per month.
5. Working days shall be eight hours for adults and six for juveniles. One day off for three.
6. All troops and reservists quartered at the mills must be withdrawn.
7. No workers to be dismissed for having taken part in anti-Japanese activities.

失业者计划
周六举行
大型集会
华商寻求
豁免虹口警捐

上海西区失业工人昨日正完成筹备失业人员大型集会的安排，目的之一是于周六集体游行至上海特区法院，要求立即释放所有被拘留的失业人员。

周二，在毛保路（音译）外东升纱厂劳工宿舍7弄8号举行了集会筹备人员的初次会议。

前该厂雇员黄达藏（Wong Ta-tsang，音译）担任主席。经过一般性讨论后，完成了召开另一次会议的安排，以便在该会议上敲定各项计划。

警方将阻止游行

预计如果失业人员试图在没有必要许可证的情况下穿过租界游行，或试图举行示威活动，国际租界警方将进行干预。

昨日，大批失业人员在渡轮路（Ferry Road，即今金陵东路附近渡口区域）以东、澳门路以南的一块空地上举行大型集会，期间他们欢迎了一位来自南京的劳工代表。

寻求免税

此地的中国商人正寻求在明日开店前豁免缴纳虹口区的警捐，并在昨日下午召开的复业委员会第二次会议上决定向上海公共租界工部局请愿，要求豁免。

关于保护该区中国商店的问题，委员会在拜访工部局秘书长费信惇（Stirling Fessenden）先生时，还口头获得了他的保证。

据悉，华人纳税会和华商地产公会均受托起草一项计划， whereby 虹口商人能最好地缓解财务困难，虽然市内其他地区的店主可能被要求缴纳租金，但虹口的商人可享受完全豁免。

今日所有中文报刊都将刊登中国商界团体的一份长篇宣言，列举导致复业的所有事件，此外还有一则简短通知，声明所有商店将于明日开业。在该宣言中，南京政府和上海公共租界工部局均因在最近的中日冲突期间未能充分保护中国商人而受到批评。

工厂重新开工

随着自中日冲突爆发以来关闭的20家纱厂和工厂重新开工，自敌对行动爆发以来，已有总计112家制造企业开门营业。

预计4月1日将有更多企业重新开工，这一天是中国商会为上海较安全地区的中国企业设定的复业日期。

养老金领取者呼吁复业

与中国商会相关的、涉及4月1日复业事宜的前雇员昨日出现在租界和法租界。他们宣读道：为了减少失业，稳定本地财政，恢复国家政府国库收入，从而增强抵抗耻辱的力量，所有位于安全地区且尚未复业的商店和工厂应于4月1日复业。

日本纱厂的前雇员鉴于工厂即将重新开工，拟定了以下要求和条件清单，作为他们考虑返回日本纱厂业主处工作的条件：

1. 发放相当于四天工资的月度奖金。此项需在复工前支付。
2. 全额发放停工期间的工资。
3. 工厂重新开工后，星期日假日全额付薪，其他假日双倍付薪。
4. 所有月薪低于30元者加薪5元，所有月薪高于30元者加薪3元。
5. 成人工作日为八小时，未成年人为六小时。每工作三天休息一天。
6. 必须撤走驻扎在纱厂的所有军队和预备役人员。
7. 不得因参与反日活动而解雇任何工人。

致，
请予关注。
所有相关人员
已通过左函通知
